MRI Report - Right Knee
Procedure: MRI of the right knee without contrast.
Clinical Indication: Mechanical knee pain and locking sensation following a sports injury.
Menisci: There is a complex, displaced tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a large flipped fragment in the intercondylar notch. The lateral meniscus is intact.
Ligaments: The anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) shows high-grade sprain with fiber discontinuity, consistent with a full-thickness tear. The posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), medial collateral ligament (MCL), and lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex are intact.
Articular Cartilage and Bone: There is mild chondromalacia of the patellofemoral compartment. A moderate-sized joint effusion is present. The visualized osseous structures show no evidence of acute fracture, but there is bone marrow edema in the lateral femoral condyle and posterior tibial plateau, suggestive of a pivot-shift contusion pattern.
Impression: Full-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). Complex, displaced tear of the medial meniscus with a large fragment. Moderate joint effusion. Bone contusions consistent with a pivot-shift injury. 
Scheduled appointments:
Urgent referral to Orthopedic Surgery for consultation. Appointment scheduled with Dr. Katherine Lee on 06/23/2025 at 2:00 PM.

Polysomnography Report
Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.
This was a technically adequate overnight diagnostic polysomnogram. Total sleep time was 345 minutes with a sleep efficiency of 82%. Sleep architecture was abnormal due to significant sleep fragmentation. REM sleep was reduced, comprising only 10% of total sleep time.
Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. These events were predominantly obstructive apneas and hypopneas, and they were more severe during REM sleep. This was associated with significant oxygen desaturation, with a nadir SpO2 of 78%. The patient's baseline oxygen saturation was 95%. No significant periodic limb movements were noted.
Impression: The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to determine the optimal pressure for treatment.
Date of Interpretation: 06/20/2025 
Interpreting Physician: Dr. Samuel Jones, MD, Dipl. ABsm

Sections show prostatic acini replaced by infiltrative, poorly-formed cribriform glands (Gleason pattern 4) and individual discrete glands (Gleason pattern 3). Gross Description:

Comments:

Biomarkers:
Immunohistochemical stains for high molecular weight cytokeratin (HMWCK) and p63 are negative in the malignant glands, supporting the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. No further molecular biomarker testing indicated on this specimen.

STOMACH, PARTIAL GASTRECTOMY:
GASTROINTESTINAL STROMAL TUMOR (GIST), SPINDLE CELL TYPE.
Tumor size: 6.5 cm.
Mitotic rate: 8 mitoses per 5 mm².
Risk of Progression: High.
Surgical margins are negative for tumor.
Microscopic Description:
Sections show a well-circumscribed but unencapsulated tumor composed of intersecting fascicles of uniform spindle cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and ovoid nuclei. There is mild to moderate nuclear atypia. The mitotic activity is brisk, counting up to 8 mitoses per 5 mm². Necrosis is not identified.
Gross Description:
Received fresh, labeled with patient's name and "partial gastrectomy," is a 12.0 x 8.0 x 5.0 cm portion of stomach. Arising from the gastric wall is a well-circumscribed, fleshy, tan-white submucosal mass measuring 6.5 x 5.8 x 5.5 cm. The tumor is 0.4 cm from the nearest surgical margin. The overlying mucosa is intact.
Comments:
The combination of tumor size (6.5 cm) and high mitotic rate (8/5 mm²) places this Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST) in the high-risk category for progressive disease. Immunohistochemical studies confirm the diagnosis, and molecular testing results are pending.

Clinical Information: 58-year-old female with a non-painful, pigmented lesion on the left cheek. The lesion has been present for approximately one year, with a recent slight increase in size. Clinical concern for atypical nevus vs. seborrheic keratosis.
Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled with the patient's name and "left cheek," is a single shave biopsy of skin measuring 0.5 x 0.4 x 0.2 cm. The specimen is a tan-brown, slightly verrucous papule. The deep margin is inked black. The specimen is bisected and submitted entirely in one cassette.
Microscopic Description: Microscopic examination reveals an exophytic proliferation of benign basaloid keratinocytes. The architecture shows prominent acanthosis, papillomatosis, and the formation of numerous keratin-filled invaginations and horn pseudocysts. The basaloid cells are uniform in appearance with small, regular nuclei and no significant mitotic activity or pleomorphism. Within the underlying dermis, there is a mild, patchy, perivascular infiltrate composed of lymphocytes and occasional eosinophils. The deep and peripheral margins are free of the lesion. No evidence of dysplasia or malignancy is identified.
Diagnosis: Skin, left cheek, shave biopsy: Seborrheic keratosis, irritated.
Comment: The histologic features are characteristic of an irritated seborrheic keratosis. The irritation corresponds to the mild dermal inflammation seen microscopically. Clinical correlation is recommended.
Specimen: One piece of skin from the left cheek, measuring 0.5 x 0.4 x 0.2 cm.
